entries.title: Press Stop twice to dictate and send
entries.body: When you are dictating, pressing Stop a second time straight after the first also sends what you said, once it has been turned into text. The button reads "Send when the words arrive" while it waits. This works in the Feedback box, in chat, in a comment follow-up, in a quiz answer and in the annotate box.

entries.title: A first open can start in Summary
entries.body: The first time you open an article in a browser while signed in, it can open with Summary's Brief view beside the text, when there is room for it. If you have experimental features switched on and there is room for that too, Marginalia is shown as well. A view you have saved, or a link that carries its own view, still wins, and going back to Plain is remembered.

entries.title: An article's purpose saves as you type
entries.body: On the page for adding an article, the box where you say what you want from it saves by itself as you type, including while the article is still being added. Add an article again and the purpose you gave before is shown, ready to edit or clear. Corrections in the profile and purpose boxes elsewhere also save more dependably.

entries.title: Clearer messages when an article cannot be fetched
entries.body: When adding an article by its address fails, the message now says more specifically what went wrong and what to try next. Retry is offered only when trying again might help. It is no longer shown for a missing page, a page that needs a login, or content the app cannot read.

entries.title: The Home icon beside the logo is gone
entries.body: When you are signed in, the changelog, privacy, contact, open source and help pages no longer show a Home icon next to the logo in the corner, which already does the same job. The profile page also loses its back arrow to the library.

entries.title: Some size-related import failures now have a fallback
entries.body: Some very long documents failed while being added, at the point where the app works out their sections, because of their size. For those failures the app now builds the contents from the document's own headings and carries on. Sections made this way have no AI-written gist, and repeated page headers and page numbers are not treated as headings.

entries.title: Chat keeps your cursor when the conversation changes
entries.body: In the chat about a passage, moving to another conversation, with Back or Forward or by picking another paragraph's chat, could leave you with no box to type in until you clicked one. The cursor now moves to the new conversation's box, unless you had already put it somewhere else.

entries.title: Marginalia shows your place above the first section
entries.body: With experimental features switched on and Marginalia showing, the top of its column was empty while you were on the title, byline or opening lines before the first section. It now shows that first section's headings and its place in the article.
